# Study overview

[Karra et al. (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2200279119) randomized
2,143 women to improved family planning access or control. The intervention
increased contraceptive use and reduced subsequent pregnancy; the adjusted
pregnancy ITT was -3.7 percentage points. Here assignment instruments endline
modern contraceptive use to estimate pregnancy effects among use compliers.
This extension is exploratory: endline use may follow pregnancy, and the
intervention may affect pregnancy through other pathways. Employment is not
available, so pregnancy is retained as the outcome. The [paper](Karra_2022.pdf)
is available locally.

# Dataset

```{r load-data}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(ivreg)
  library(sandwich)
  library(princeBART)
  library(future)
  library(posterior)
})

load("processed_data.rda")
head(dat, 5)
```

- **Outcome (`next_preg_2018`):** pregnancy since the index birth by the 2018 interview.
- **Treatment (`curr_use_inj_adj`):** endline modern contraceptive use.
- **Instrument (`treatment`):** randomized assignment to family planning access.
- **Covariates:** baseline contraceptive use, pregnancy, area, age group, age at
  sexual debut, living children, ever use, education, work, religion, and ethnicity.
  `exposure` is included only in the original ITT replication.

# Objective 1: Pregnancy among contraceptive-use compliers

## Reproduce the original ITT

Use the authors' adjusted pregnancy specification in `DO_3_MAIN_RESULTS.do`,
with available cases and an HC1 robust, t-based 95% confidence interval.

```{r reproduce-itt}
fit_itt <- lm(
  next_preg_2018 ~ treatment + exposure + preg_bl + area_bl + age_group_bl +
    sex_age_bl + total_alive_bl + ever_use_bl + edu_primary_bl + work_bl +
    religion_r_bl + ethnicity_r_bl,
  data = dat, na.action = na.omit
)
itt_estimate <- unname(coef(fit_itt)["treatment"])
itt_se <- sqrt(vcovHC(fit_itt, type = "HC1")["treatment", "treatment"])
itt_result <- c(itt_estimate,
                itt_estimate + qt(c(0.025, 0.975), df.residual(fit_itt)) * itt_se)
```

## 2SLS analysis

The IV models use the same complete-case sample and baseline covariates.
The 95% confidence interval uses HC1 robust standard errors and normal quantiles.

```{r two-stage-least-squares}
dat <- dat |>
  select(-exposure) |>
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.x))) |>
  droplevels()
fit_iv <- ivreg(
  next_preg_2018 ~ curr_use_inj_adj + curr_use_inj_adj_bl + preg_bl + area_bl +
    age_group_bl + sex_age_bl + total_alive_bl + ever_use_bl + edu_primary_bl +
    work_bl + religion_r_bl + ethnicity_r_bl |
    treatment + curr_use_inj_adj_bl + preg_bl + area_bl + age_group_bl +
    sex_age_bl + total_alive_bl + ever_use_bl + edu_primary_bl + work_bl +
    religion_r_bl + ethnicity_r_bl,
  data = dat
)
iv_estimate <- unname(coef(fit_iv)["curr_use_inj_adj"])
iv_se <- sqrt(vcovHC(fit_iv, type = "HC1")["curr_use_inj_adj", "curr_use_inj_adj"])
iv_result <- c(iv_estimate, iv_estimate + qnorm(c(0.025, 0.975)) * iv_se)
```

## princeBART approach

Report the mixed complier effect with a 95% equal-tail credible interval.

```{r princebart}
plan(multisession, workers = 4)
set.seed(20261102)
fit_ps <- prince_BART(
  next_preg_2018 ~ curr_use_inj_adj_bl + preg_bl + area_bl + age_group_bl +
    sex_age_bl + total_alive_bl + ever_use_bl + edu_primary_bl + work_bl +
    religion_r_bl + ethnicity_r_bl | treatment | curr_use_inj_adj,
  data = dat, uptake_type = "binary", n_chains = 4, workers = 4,
  n_warmup = 500, n_samples = 1000, n_trees = 50, keep_trees = FALSE
)
plan(sequential)

effect_chains <- lapply(fit_ps$chains, function(chain) {
  pc <- 1 - chain$p_a - chain$p_n
  rowSums(pc * (chain$m_y1c - chain$m_y0c)) / rowSums(pc)
})
tau <- unlist(effect_chains, use.names = FALSE)
bart_result <- c(mean(tau), quantile(tau, c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE))
effect_draws <- as_draws_array(array(
  unlist(effect_chains), c(length(effect_chains[[1]]), length(effect_chains), 1),
  dimnames = list(NULL, NULL, "Complier effect")
))
summarise_draws(effect_draws) |> select(variable, rhat, ess_bulk, ess_tail)
```

## Comparison

Effects are percentage-point changes in pregnancy risk. Published and reproduced
ITT estimates concern assignment; the IV methods concern contraceptive-use
compliers. Their estimands and samples differ. Follow-up duration also varies,
so this is not a fixed 24-month pregnancy endpoint.

```{r comparison}
comparison <- tibble(
  Method = c("Published adjusted ITT", "Reproduced adjusted ITT", "2SLS complier effect",
             "princeBART mixed complier effect"),
  Estimate_pp = 100 * c(-0.037, itt_result[1], iv_result[1], bart_result[1]),
  Lower_pp = 100 * c(-0.0621, itt_result[2], iv_result[2], bart_result[2]),
  Upper_pp = 100 * c(-0.0111, itt_result[3], iv_result[3], bart_result[3]),
  Interval = c("95% CI", "95% CI", "95% CI", "95% CrI")
)
comparison
```

## Effect heterogeneity

A shallow tree summarizes fitted conditional effects over baseline covariates.
These exploratory segments do not resolve the timing or exclusion assumptions.

```{r heterogeneity}
segments <- segment_heterogeneity(
  fit_ps,
  rpart_control = rpart::rpart.control(cp = 0, maxdepth = 2),
  min_compliers_bucket = 30, ci_level = 0.95, plot = TRUE
)
as_tibble(segments$effects) |>
  select(segment, mean, ci_lower, ci_upper, n, n_group)
segments$plot$effect
```
